nodes.body: This inner join silently drops any `cards` row that has no `card_entries` row. The schema does not enforce the opening-entry invariant, so a damaged or externally-created database can contain such a Card; `Reader::queue()` then returns a successful queue that omits it instead of surfacing corruption, contrary to the documented “every Card” result and the console’s complete-read behavior. Detect the missing latest entry as corruption (or otherwise fail the queue) rather than filtering the Card out.

Adding `Unavailable` makes the public taxonomy five-way, but the `ErrorCategory` documentation immediately above still calls it a four-way taxonomy. Consumers of the new bind/startup/serve failures will receive a value the documented contract does not describe; update the public taxonomy documentation (and the CLI category description) to match the enum.

### 🟡 Changes recommended Moderate findings remain in selected-entry error handling, missing-entry detection, and pinned Playwright invocation. *Once you've addressed the issues Copilot identified, you can request another Copilot review.*

This makes one fixture value drift-prone and violates the repository’s load-bearing-literal convention; name the port once and derive the expected authorities from that constant. **crates/daemar-card/src/console.rs:489** * This is the only selected-entry path that discards `entry_view` failures. If `history_fields()` fails while building the inspector, the handler still returns a 200 Card page with the inspector silently omitted, instead of the documented whole-page storage error used for `card.entries` above.
